column1: # Spanish grammar words. One line per word as written + part of speech:
# word <TAB> UD part of speech <TAB> senses separated by " | ".
# The file replaces Wiktionary's determiner, pronoun, preposition, conjunction,
# particle and auxiliary entries for every word listed here; nouns, verbs,
# adverbs and other content words stay (`de` the letter, `son` "tone"), unless
# a line lists that part of speech too. A word's lines come first in the
# popover, in this file's order, so its commonest use goes first. Case matters.
# Irregular verb forms a reader can't connect to their infinitive get lines of
# their own (`tiene` "has", `hizo` "did"): the protocol has no inflection
# tables. "→ tener" links the line to its verb, which the popover still shows
# after it; a VERB line replaces Wiktionary's other verbs for the word.
# Forms whose noun or adverb is as common are left out (`vino` "wine",
# Each sense explains what the word does, for a learner reading it next to
# the sentence: what it expresses, then the English, then a short phrase in
# brackets when the English alone doesn't settle it ("is, for where something
# is or how it is right now: he's at home (está en casa)"). No notes on case
# or position: the sentence shows those.
# A form names its base word, which links it: "form of tener: has → tener".
